lines: At the edge of a forest, a researcher has ten years of data and one urgent question.
In a village square, a community worker has 300 families to reach before dark.
In a room full of files, a data lead guards records that could save lives, or expose them.
By a broken bridge, a tech worker is stuck with a tool nobody can fix.
Four people. One road. 2,100 km. Your choices decide how they get there.
coldOpen.title: THE RIDE
coldOpen.note: Let each line land in silence before the next. About 45 seconds in all. The engine idles underneath; mute it from Sound if the room is loud.

crew.label: Leading the ride
crew.title: Tech4Good Community
crew.line: A community of builders who help social-impact organisations use technology with care, and build it themselves.

crew.closing: But we can't make this ride alone. We'll need you, and the people we meet on the road.
crew.note: About 60 seconds. Say who Tech4Good is in one breath, then the three facts, then the closing line.

ignition.phone: We're off. Listen to the story.
ignition.note: Ask the room if they're ready, then fire it up.

stops.voice: Before we set off, someone shared two websites with us. They made us stop and look twice.

sites.title: Holématthi Nature Foundation
sites.builtBy: PLACEHOLDER: who built the Holématthi site
sites.took: PLACEHOLDER: how long the Holématthi site took
sites.cost: PLACEHOLDER: what the Holématthi site cost
sites.caption: Book → digital

steps.note: Open either site live from here if the room wants a closer look. Then ask who built them.

steps.question: Who do you think built these?

options.text: Someone with no coding background, using AI

steps.note: A quick guess, not a question. Show the room's guesses and don't reveal yet.

steps.question: If anyone can build something like this, what becomes the hardest part?
steps.revealNote: Neither had a development team. The hard part has moved from writing code to choosing the right problem.
steps.core: AI has collapsed the time and cost of building; non-developers ship real things. The bottleneck is now choosing the right problem.

stops.handover: If the hard part is the problem, we should go where the problems are.

stops.voice: I have 4,000 camera-trap photos and ten years of notes on cattle lost to tigers. I want to know where the next attack is likely, before it happens.

steps.question: AI says the next attacks will be in three villages. What do you do?

options.text: Check it against Meera's field knowledge
Send it straight to the villagers
Ignore it; AI can't know a forest

steps.revealNote: The three villages are the only ones with mobile signal. That's where the reports came from.
steps.core: AI finds patterns only in the data it's given. Gaps and bias become confident answers, and AI can invent things outright. A prediction isn't a decision: people who know the ground check it.

stops.handover: Even if the warning is right, it's useless if it doesn't reach people. Lakshmi knows how.

stops.voice: When a warning comes, I have to reach 300 families. Half have basic phones, many can't read, and the signal drops after dark.

steps.question: What's the best way to get the warning to them?

options.text: An SMS in the local language
A voice call in the local language
Lakshmi and volunteers, with AI drafting the messages

steps.revealNote: There's no single answer, but the app is the one that fails here.
steps.core: Accessibility means language, literacy, devices and connectivity, not just disability. Shape technology around people. AI can support the humans who reach them.

stops.handover: To reach families, I keep names, phone numbers and addresses. Arif deals with that every day.

steps.question: Does your team use AI today?
steps.note: A quick pulse, not a question. Every answer adds fuel. Skip it if time is short.

stops.voice: We have records for 40 clinics. AI could spot which mothers are at risk before it's too late. But every record has a name, a phone number and a diagnosis.

steps.question: What should AI be allowed to see to spot the risk?

options.text: Records with names and phones removed
Records with identities swapped for tokens

steps.core: Share only what the question needs. Removing names isn't enough: age + village + diagnosis can identify someone. Tokens keep analysis useful while identities stay home.

steps.title: Swap names for tokens
steps.text: AI works with the tokens. The key that links them back stays with you. It lowers the risk, it doesn't erase it.
steps.note: Tokenised is not the same as anonymous. Whoever holds the key can link it back.

steps.question: Where should the AI run?

options.text: Cloud AI, under a data agreement

steps.revealNote: Local AI keeps data in-house but needs hardware, skills and upkeep. Cloud AI is more capable, so read the terms.
steps.core: Open-source models can run on your own machines. Local isn't automatically safe: access, logs and backups still matter.

steps.title: Insight Out by Tech4Good
steps.text: Questions like these are what Insight Out explores: making AI useful for social-impact work while taking data, privacy and infrastructure seriously.
steps.note: Point people to Insight Out if they want to take these questions further.

stops.handover: Whatever we set up, someone has to keep it running. Ravi knows what happens when nobody does.

stops.voice: Two years ago, a college team built us an app for crop prices. They graduated. Now it's broken, nobody has the password, and farmers still call me about it.

steps.question: Before anyone relies on a tool, what must be in place? Pick three.

options.text: Who owns the code and passwords
Who fixes it when it breaks
Where the data is stored and backed up
Written notes on how it works
Whether an open-source tool already does it

steps.revealNote: AI makes building fast, and abandoning things fast too. Ownership, notes, costs and backups decide whether a tool survives.
steps.core: Custom vs. open source: is 80% already solved by something that exists?

steps.question: Which traveller is your organisation missing most?
steps.core: No single person or organisation has all four. That's what communities are for: borrowing the traveller you're missing.

steps.text: Nobody gets here alone. Technology helps us travel faster; the people we travel with decide where we go.
steps.note: Slow down for this one. End on the last line.
